Space & Defense Daily — Friday, Oct 30, 2026

The EU opened a €21.3 billion second round of SAFE defence loans. The US Army picked Lockheed Martin for its Future Interceptor program, worth more than $1 billion. NATO's Black Sea allies condemned drone attacks on shipping after another vessel was hit off Bulgaria.

Here's your space and defense news for Friday, Oct 30.

Top stories: The EU opened a €21.3 billion second round of SAFE defence loans. The US Army picked Lockheed Martin for its Future Interceptor program, worth more than $1 billion. NATO's Black Sea allies condemned drone attacks on shipping after another vessel was hit off Bulgaria.

NATO

  • NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte told the national armaments directors' meeting (CNAD) to "turn commitments into contracts," building on the Ankara Summit decisions. The talks covered faster production, procurement reform and deep precision strike. NATO on the armaments directors
  • NATO's innovation accelerator, DIANA, signed a memorandum with Ukraine, its first with any NATO partner. It opens joint technology development and testing and helps Ukrainian innovators meet NATO requirements. NATO on DIANA and Ukraine
  • Bulgaria signed on to NATO's joint project to buy and field defences against drones and cruise missiles. NATO on Bulgaria
  • The defence ministers of Bulgaria, Romania and Turkey condemned attacks on commercial ships in the Black Sea and agreed to share more intelligence and early warning. During their Oct. 28 meeting, a drone boat hit the container ship Contship Jet off Bulgaria. Defense News on the Black Sea

European Union

  • The Commission opened the second SAFE loan call, worth €21.3 billion and open to all member states. Priorities are air and missile defence, drones and counter-drone systems, and ammunition, and joint buying with Ukraine is encouraged. About €13.5 billion of the first round has been paid out so far. European Commission
  • At NATO's FUSE event in Riga, Commissioner Dombrovskis announced the first two EU drone technology hubs, in Latvia and the Netherlands, opening in 2027 under the DECODER project. He also said the EU aims to sign a defence industry pact with Ukraine by the end of 2026. Kyiv Independent on drone hubs
  • The EU–Canada summit opened in Montreal. A draft statement promises Canada talks on access to Galileo services, explores Canadian participation in IRIS², and covers Arctic and critical-materials cooperation. Defense News on the summit
  • Officials on both sides are pushing for a broad upgrade while Trump is focused on the midterms. Politico Europe
  • OCCAR, the European agency that manages joint arms programs, ordered 69 more Schakal wheeled infantry fighting vehicles for Germany (35) and the Netherlands (34). Rheinmetall's share is in the mid-hundreds of millions of euros. Rheinmetall
  • Outside the EU, Britain will require foreign suppliers that win selected defence contracts over £50 million to deliver UK jobs or investment. It will decide case by case starting April 2027. Reuters via Yahoo Finance

United States

  • The Army chose Lockheed Martin for its Future Interceptor program, worth more than $1 billion, with Lockheed paying $423 million and the Army about $660 million. Lockheed's PAC-3 Edge is due to start testing in 2027 and deploy by 2031. DefenseScoop
  • Defense Secretary Hegseth removed Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Joint Staff's strategy and plans director, accusing him of leaking classified information on the Iran and Ukraine wars. NBC News on Sylvia
  • The administration's record $1.5 trillion defense budget request has stalled in Congress, held back by frustration over Iran and over Hegseth. Washington Post
  • The Nov. 3 midterms could reshape the planned surge in Space Force spending and Golden Dome missile defense investment. SpaceNews on the midterms
  • The NRO is rethinking how it buys commercial radar satellite imagery, as demand grows and suppliers press for more predictable revenue. SpaceNews on the NRO
  • The Air Force Research Lab plans a $30 million "Cislunar Prime" challenge: 15 small-business contracts of $2 million each for tracking, communications and navigation beyond geosynchronous orbit. Awards would start next spring. Air & Space Forces Magazine
  • A medium drone boat has deployed for the first time, with the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group. Navy leaders want these boats to become a routine part of fleet operations, with 30 due by the end of FY2027. Defense News on drone boats
  • NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said Artemis III "must fly" in 2027 to test docking with the Blue Origin and SpaceX landers ahead of a 2028 Moon landing. He also said he would expect to be fired if China gets there first. USA Today

European space

  • Airbus CEO Guillaume Faury said Airbus could join the UK–Japan–Italy GCAP fighter program after the Franco-German fighter project collapsed. He said governments should decide soon. Euronews
  • From Oct. 27: ESA ordered four more second-generation Galileo satellites, two each from Thales Alenia Space and Airbus. That brings the fleet to 16, with delivery in 2031. ESA

Global space & defense

  • A Russian jet-powered drone hit a busy platform at Dnipro's train station, killing at least 14 people. Separately, Moscow said it shot down 613 Ukrainian drones aimed at the capital overnight. Al Jazeera
  • EU Council President Costa called for more pressure on Russia. Ukraine has paused strikes on Russian refineries under US pressure, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The Guardian
  • Telesat pushed full global Lightspeed service back to mid-2028 because launch capacity is tight. Arctic service for the Canadian military is still planned for Q1 2028. CEO Dan Goldberg said the recent Starlink disruptions in Ukraine have increased government interest. Via Satellite
  • Chinese commercial launch company Landspace won a tender to launch what is believed to be the reusable Haolong cargo spaceplane for the Tiangong station. SpaceNews on Landspace
  • North Korea fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from near Wonsan into the sea, its first launch since Oct. 12. NBC News/Reuters
  • Canada released its first national security strategy since 2004, built around sovereignty and rearming its armed forces. Breaking Defense
  • A few items were behind paywalls, so they're based on the headline and summary only: the Washington Post story, NBC's story on Sylvia, and both SpaceNews military pieces.
